text: Databases are organised systems for storing and managing information. In a relational database, data is kept in tables made up of rows and columns. To get information from these tables, you use queries written in SQL, a standard language for asking questions about your data. Before building a database, you need data modeling to plan how tables connect to each other. Indexes help speed up searches by allowing the database to find rows quickly. However, not all databases use tables. NoSQL databases store data differently, often as documents or key-value pairs, and they are useful when data changes fast or does not fit neatly into tables.
